classification.difficultyReason: Infer an intersection from the union, then find the B-only probability; compare with the mutually exclusive case.

content.prompt:
Two events, $A$ and $B$, are such that $P(A)=\frac{3}{5}$ and $P(B)=\frac{1}{4}$.

If $A'$ denotes the complement of $A$, calculate $P(A'\cap B)$ when:

spec.description: Universal-set rectangle with overlapping circles A and B. Only the B-only region is shaded. Ordinary blue source outlines and labels become black.
spec.mathematics: Intersection probability 1/10; B-only probability 3/20. A-only and outside regions have no numerical labels.

spec.description: Universal-set rectangle with separate circles A and B. B alone is shaded. Ordinary blue source outlines and labels become black.
spec.mathematics: Disjoint events with probabilities 3/5 in A and 1/4 in B; A prime intersection B equals B.
